world_models.summary: V compresses each feature row to a latent, M (an LSTM with a mixture-density head) learns how latents follow each other, and a tiny linear controller C on [z; h] is searched by CMA-ES for net reward.
world_models.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is C's softmax share of long over long + short; the market does not react to the agent, so it maximises cost-aware reward on the training span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost) with its own position left out of its state. Differs from the spec: V encodes feature rows, not pixels; C is scored on the real training tape, not in M's dream; M takes no action input. Expect: imagination adds no information beyond the learned feature dynamics; the controller is linear, so it trades a few directions of the latent.

native.produces: A position action from a tiny linear controller that reads a latent code of the current observation made by a variational autoencoder together with the hidden state of a recurrent mixture-density network that predicts how that code evolves, and with them a generative model able to dream latent sequences.
native.targetVariable: The position to hold at each bar, chosen to maximise cumulative reward, alongside the distribution of the next latent code.
native.objectiveNote: The three parts are trained apart: the vision part on reconstruction plus a Kullback-Leibler term, the memory part by maximum likelihood of the next code under a mixture of Gaussians, and the controller last by a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy or policy gradients on cumulative reward in real or dreamed rollouts; the memory part is action-conditioned because it takes the previous action as an input, and it predicts latent codes, not prices.

metrics.why: The vision and memory parts never see reward, so the only place the whole stack is judged is the average reward of the linear controller's action on bars that neither it nor the two representation parts were fitted on.
metrics.baseline: The same controller staying flat on every bar, which earns nothing, and buy and hold on the same series.

metrics.why: A controller trained inside the memory part's dream is only as good as the dream, so the error of the recurrent mixture-density network's prediction of the latent code several steps ahead, with no real bar fed in between, says how long a dream can be trusted, measured in units of the code.
metrics.baseline: The persistence forecast that the latent code stays where it is, at the same steps ahead.

metrics.why: The specification's chief risk is a controller that overfits unrealistic dream rollouts, and the reward it earns inside the memory part's dream minus the reward it earns on real bars is the direct measure of that.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value when the dream and the real tape pay the controller the same.

metrics.why: The memory part is trained by maximum likelihood to place a mixture of Gaussians over the next latent code, so the log density it gives to the codes of unseen bars is its own objective read out of sample, stated as an exact density of the code and not of the bar.
metrics.baseline: The log density given to the same codes by a single Gaussian centred on the current code with the training spread of one-bar changes.

metrics.why: The evolution strategy draws a fresh population of controllers every generation and the mixture-density network samples its dreams, so the final controller differs from seed to seed and one run is not yet a result.
metrics.baseline: The same three-part agent on the same series with only the seed changed.

metrics.why: The controller is found by black-box search and not by gradients, so the best cumulative reward found so far against the number of generations shows whether the search had flattened out or was stopped while still climbing.
Every generation scores a whole population of candidate controllers on the same training reward, and the more candidates were scored the more the winner's training reward is inflated by luck.

If the weighted divergence term of the vision part pushes the code all the way onto its prior, the code stops depending on the bar and both the memory part and the controller are left reading noise, so the term is watched apart from the reconstruction error.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value at which the code has collapsed onto its prior and carries nothing about the bar.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The registry's Sharpe ratio measures the Model Cycle's trading rule driven by the controller's preferred side and is reported as run, while natively the controller is judged by the reward of its own action.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: It is a downside figure of the engine's simulated equity path and sits in the as-run record, because the controller's search fitness is cumulative reward with no downside term.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: The drawdown comes from the engine marking positions to market along the test span and is an as-run number that none of the three parts is trained on or defines.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: It is computed from trades the engine closes under its own rule and belongs to the as-run record, not to the vision, memory and controller stack.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: It is a position sizing rule and not a measurement, and the linear controller outputs an action without any Kelly calculation.

notApplicable.name: Policy Entropy
notApplicable.why: The specification's controller maps its inputs to one action through a linear layer and is not a distribution over actions, so it has no entropy to report.

notApplicable.name: Held-out reconstruction error
notApplicable.why: As a verdict on the agent it misleads, because the vision part can rebuild every bar faithfully while the code it produces is of no use to the controller.

notApplicable.name: Critic explained variance
notApplicable.why: The controller is searched by an evolution strategy on cumulative reward and has no value function whose estimates could be compared with realised returns.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable agent keeps the specification's three parts, a variational autoencoder for vision, a recurrent mixture-density network for memory and a linear controller searched by a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy, but vision encodes one row of feature columns at a time and not an image, memory takes no action as input, and the controller is scored on the real training tape's net reward with an entropy bonus and never inside memory's dream; the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state, so the as-run numbers measure cost-aware direction calls made by a linear readout of the learned code and hidden state.
asRun.probabilityNote: The linear controller turns the latest latent code joined with the memory network's hidden state into scores for short, flat and long, and the probability of up is the softmax long share divided by the sum of the long and short shares, with the flat share discarded and nothing fitted to outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: during the vision and memory epochs the summed evidence lower bound loss, mixture negative log-likelihood of the next code and squared reward error with no validation value; during the controller generations minus the best training-tape fitness found so far in move-scale reward units, with nats of the long share on validation rows

meaningful.why: The linear controller is the only part searched for net reward, on whole trades of the training tape, so the money made by trading the side it prefers between long and short is the as-run number nearest to its fitness, read with the agent's own flat choice overridden.

It measures how steadily the controller's preferred side earned money per bar after costs, which tests whether the few directions of the code and hidden state a linear map can trade hold up beyond the training tape.

A linear controller with a bias term can score well on a rising training tape by preferring long everywhere, and removing what holding the contract made on the same folds shows whether the code and hidden state added to that.

The search fitness is a mean of separately paid decisions and gives no weight to losses that arrive in a row, so the deepest hole on the marked-to-market path is a risk the evolution strategy never scored.

It sets what the winning trades opened by the controller's preferred side made against what the losing ones lost after costs, read with the trade count because a controller dominated by its bias seldom changes side.
It gives the share of trades opened on a change of the controller's preferred side that closed in profit, which describes the shape of the result while the engine's holding rule decides each exit.
The controller reads the latest latent code directly, so bar-to-bar jitter in the code can flip its preferred side, and this turnover shows how much of the result that jitter gave away in costs.
It counts how often the controller's long score crossed its short score or a holding period ended in a flip, and every trading number of this agent is read with it.
It shows how often the controller preferred long to short, which reveals a search that settled on the bias term alone and left the code and hidden state unused.

The hard call is up whenever the long share is at least the short share, so the hit rate tests whether the side the evolution strategy tuned the controller to prefer is also the side price went, against calling the fold's training majority direction.
Averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars shows whether the controller's preference really follows the code and hidden state or is a one-sided lean credited by a trending test span.
It gives one symmetric number for whether the controller's preferred side moves with the actual direction, where zero means its linear readout carries nothing beyond a constant lean.

The long share is a smooth function of the controller's score gap, so this checks whether bars where that gap leans further to long are more often up bars, using the ordering alone and not reading the share as odds.

The price line is a small head on the same latent code and hidden state the controller reads, in a second fit of vision and memory on the price target, so its skill against forecasting no move tests whether that state holds a real forecast of size.
It states in points the typical miss of the price head sitting on the code and hidden state, read beside the miss of the no-change forecast on the same bars.

It checks the sign of a forecast made by a small nonlinear head on the code and hidden state with no costs involved, so it can disagree with the linear controller's side and shows what the state offers beyond a linear readout.

During the controller generations the training curve holds the best tape fitness found so far, so it shows whether the evolution strategy had flattened out or was cut off by the patience rule while still improving.

The kept generation is the one whose long share, turned into a position between fully short and fully long, earned the highest mean net reward on the validation tape, so the figure is flattered by the choosing and read only beside the test result.

It is the score that chose the learning rate of vision and memory, the only searched setting of this agent, on blocks inside the training span, and it is optimistic because it is the best of the trials.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The long share is a softmax of a linear controller tuned for net reward plus an entropy bonus and was never fitted to how often price rises, so scoring it as odds measures how far the search pushed the scores apart and not honesty.
It grades the long share as a probability of an up bar, while the controller was searched to earn reward on the tape, so its value says nothing about the agent's decisions.
Calibration compares stated odds with observed frequencies, and the controller's action shares were never meant to equal the frequency of up bars.
The slope of outcomes on the log-odds of the long share reads the scale of the controller's weights left by the search and the entropy coefficient, not an over-confident or timid forecaster.
It rests on the Brier score of a preference share and on a hindsight up share of the test bars, neither of which the controller stated.

The training curve switches from the vision and memory loss to minus the controller's tape fitness while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference never compares like with like.
With the long-only setting off the engine never goes flat once in a trade, so this share reflects the engine overriding the flat action and not how often the controller wanted a position.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and the agent's position is not in the state, so each decision is rewarded as one fixed trade over the label horizon and nothing in training resembles managing an open position.

The engine overrides the agent's own flat action, its sizing and its holding period: the traded side is long whenever the long share is at least the short share, even on bars where flat was the controller's most preferred action.

The memory network takes no action as input and the controller is scored on the real training tape and not in a dream, so nothing is learned in imagination and the model adds only the feature dynamics it compressed.

No validation value exists during the vision and memory epochs, so the kept state is always one of the controller generations, and the patience rule can end the evolution strategy early when validation reward stops improving.
The training curve changes meaning partway through the run, from the vision and memory loss to minus the best controller fitness, so it must not be read as one falling curve.

The price line comes from a second fit of vision and memory with a price head and no controller, selected on validation Huber loss, so the price forecast numbers test the learned state and say nothing about the controller.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because targets overlap across the label horizon, so intervals around these numbers need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than MNQ the costs charged are the MNQ account figures, a stated assumption, and the last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.

recurrent_state_space_model.summary: A recurrent state-space model (a deterministic GRU path plus a stochastic latent with prior and posterior) learns the window's dynamics, reward and session breaks; an actor-critic reads its state.
recurrent_state_space_model.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the actor-critic's share of long over long + short on the RSSM state; the market does not react to the agent, so it maximises cost-aware reward on the training span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost) with its own position left out of its state. Differs from the spec: no action input to the transition; the actor-critic uses every action's known tape reward (all-action gradient); no overshooting. Expect: the state rebuilt from the window each bar; edge only from learned feature dynamics.

native.produces: A latent state made of a deterministic recurrent memory and a sampled stochastic part, with a prior that predicts the next stochastic part from memory alone, a posterior that also sees the new bar, and decoders for the bar and the reward.
native.targetVariable: the next bar's feature row and the reward, described through the latent state, so that the prior can roll the state forward without new bars
native.objectiveNote: The recurrent state-space model's own loss is an evidence lower bound: reconstruction and reward log-likelihood plus a weighted Kullback-Leibler divergence between posterior and prior with a free-bits floor; in the specification the recurrence is conditioned on the previous action and the decoders predict the bar and the reward from the latent state.

metrics.why: The whole point of splitting the state into a recurrent memory and a sampled part is that the prior can be unrolled with no new bars, so the error of that blind rollout at each step ahead says how far imagination can be trusted; the decoder lets it be stated in feature units.
metrics.baseline: carrying the last observed bar forward unchanged on the same series

metrics.why: The model is fitted by variational inference, so its own score out of sample is the evidence lower bound on unseen sequences, reported as a lower bound on the log-likelihood and named as such, with the free-bits floor removed.
metrics.baseline: the same lower bound on the fold's training sequences

metrics.why: The specification stops at the latent state and leaves the planner or actor-critic open, so the reward earned on unseen bars only exists once a controller reads the recurrent memory and the sampled part; it then shows whether that state was useful for the decision.
metrics.baseline: the flat action, which earns zero on the same tape

metrics.why: Because the specified recurrence takes the previous action, a controller can be scored inside prior rollouts; reward expected there minus reward paid by the tape shows whether the reward decoder flatters the policy.
metrics.baseline: a gap of zero, meaning imagination and the tape agree

metrics.why: The reward decoder reads the same recurrent memory and stochastic part as everything else, so its forecast of the coming move is a real point forecast that can be compared with forecasting no move at all.
metrics.baseline: the no-change forecast on the same resolved bars

metrics.why: Reported apart from reconstruction, the divergence between posterior and prior shows whether the stochastic part carries anything: pinned at the free-bits floor it means the posterior has stopped listening to the bar.
metrics.baseline: the configured free-bits floor

metrics.why: Counting the stochastic units whose posterior mean actually moves from bar to bar tells how much of the sampled half of the state is alive in a quiet market, where the specification warns of collapse.
metrics.baseline: the configured size of the stochastic latent

metrics.why: The reconstruction, reward and divergence terms are drawn per step to see that Kullback-Leibler balancing kept neither side from collapsing; the curve shows convergence and is never a score.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable agent implements the recurrent state-space model with its deterministic gated recurrent path, stochastic latent, prior, posterior and decoders for the bar, the reward and the session break, trained with free bits, but the recurrence takes no action, there is no overshooting, and the state is rebuilt from a zero start over the last window at every bar; an actor-critic that is shown every action's known tape reward then reads that state without sending gradient back. The market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state, so the as-run numbers measure whether the long-versus-short preference learned on the training tape matches the close-to-close direction on later bars.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the actor-critic's share of long over long plus short, the sigmoid of the long logit minus the short logit, read from the recurrent memory joined with the posterior mean of the stochastic latent at the window's last bar; no sampling happens at prediction and nothing fits the share to outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: training: reconstruction, reward error, session-break cross-entropy, weighted divergence with free bits and actor-critic loss added together in mixed units; validation: nats per scored validation bar

meaningful.why: The actor-critic on the recurrent state was trained on tape reward net of the round-trip cost, and this is the matching result on unseen bars under the engine's rule: long when the long share is at least one half, short otherwise, with the agent's flat action and sizing overridden.

It sets the sign of the preference read from the recurrent memory and stochastic latent against the realised direction in one symmetric number, the only part of the policy output that drives the trades.
Subtracting buy and hold on the same folds separates what the state-dependent switching earned from a simple long lean picked up in a rising training span.
It compares the per-bar profit of calls read from the recurrent state with their swing under the engine's always-in-the-market rule, so it grades the call's sign plus that rule.
It shows the deepest losing stretch of the calls; because the state is rebuilt from the same overlapping window each bar, the preference changes slowly and can sit through a long adverse run.
A trade ends when the preference read from the recurrent state flips, so winning over losing trade money after costs shows whether those flips were well timed.
The share of profitable closed trades describes how the flips of the state-reading policy resolved, read with the trade count since a smooth state flips rarely.

The share of scored bars where the preferred side of the state-reading policy matched the realised direction, to be set against the fold's majority-class accuracy because the policy can lean to the training drift.

The share of scored bars that fall in the fold's training majority class is what a policy earns by leaning with the training drift, so the accuracy of the policy that reads the recurrent state is read against it on the same fold.

A trade closes when the preference read from the recurrent state flips or the fold ends, and a smooth state flips rarely, so the count of closed trades shows how few decisions the profit and the win rate rest on.

The best learning-rate trial's search score minus the same quantity on the fold's test walk shows how much of the selection score the recurrent state-space agent failed to carry to unseen bars; it sits beside the search objective value, which is optimistic by construction.
Averaging the hit rate on up bars and down bars reveals a policy on the recurrent state that calls one side nearly always.
The long share varies continuously with the recurrent state, so the ranking shows whether a stronger long lean went with more up bars, independent of the share's scale.

It tests a return head on the recurrent memory and stochastic latent of a second fit of the same model, trained jointly on the price target, against forecasting no move; it shows what this state can forecast, not what the traded policy's weights know.
The average miss in points of the return head on the separately fitted recurrent state, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars.
Whether the return head on the separately fitted state gets the sign of the move right; as a different fit from the actor-critic it may disagree with the traded call.
The share of bars on which the state-reading policy prefers long shows whether the result is one directional bet or real switching.
The spread of the long share shows how far the actor departs from one half; the entropy bonus holds it close, so a tiny spread means calls decided by very small preferences.
Only the learning rate is searched for this agent, on inner blocks of the training span, and the best trial's score is a selection score that is optimistic by construction.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The long share comes from a reward-trained actor with an entropy bonus and was never fitted to the frequency of up bars, so its logarithmic loss does not grade stated odds.
Squared distance between a policy's long share and the outcome treats a preference as a probability forecast, which it is not.
No step links a long share of a given size to an up frequency of that size, so the calibration bins mostly reflect the entropy bonus.
The slope on the log-odds of a policy share measures the actor's sharpness, set by the entropy coefficient, not honesty of odds.
The training curve is the summed world-model and actor-critic loss and the validation curve is logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference compares unrelated quantities.
With long-only off and no stop or target the engine never goes flat after the first call, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the policy's flat action.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state.
The agent's flat action, its sizing and its holding period are overridden: the engine trades every bar long or short by the sign of the long share.

The agent is trained on the move from the next bar's open to the open after the holding period, net of the round-trip cost, while the classification metrics score the close-to-close move over the label horizon.
The kept epoch is the one with the best validation reward of the position implied by the long share, so validation numbers are optimistic and only the test walk is out of sample.
The prior is never rolled forward as run: no imagined rollout feeds the controller, so nothing here tests the model's imagination.
The price forecast comes from a second fit of the same architecture with a return head, not from the weights that produce the traded call.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because horizons overlap, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq future the cost charged is the Micro Nasdaq account figure, applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable agent is a variational recurrent network with a prior from the past context, a posterior from the new bar, a decoder, a reward head and a divergence weight ramped up over the first epochs in place of a free-bits floor, but it takes no action anywhere and the probability of up is not the share of sampled futures that end higher: an actor-critic shown every action's known tape reward reads the recurrent context without sending gradient back. metrics.why: The specification names its own reference: the same planner working on the raw, ungrouped state; the abstraction earns its place only if the plan on abstract states does at least as well on the same folds.
metrics.baseline: the same planner on the raw feature state of the same series

metrics.why: The abstract transition model says which abstract state follows which, and a plan several steps deep is only as good as that chain; the error is stated as the miss between predicted and realised abstract state at each step ahead, in latent distance, or as the share of wrong groups once the grouping is made hard.
metrics.baseline: predicting that the bar stays in its current abstract state

metrics.why: This applies once the grouping is made hard, as in the specification's Hard-Partition variant. The specification warns that the grouping can collapse onto similarities that exist only inside the training window; refitting with another seed or on the next fold and checking that the same bars land together tests that directly.
metrics.baseline: the agreement expected from random grouping, which the index sets to zero

metrics.why: This applies once the grouping is made hard, as in the specification's Hard-Partition variant. Bisimulation groups bars by what follows them, so on unseen bars each abstract state should show its own up share; states that all sit on the series average were grouped by something other than behaviour.
metrics.baseline: the up share of all scored bars of the same series

metrics.why: Whatever plans on the abstract model picks the action with the highest estimated value, and a maximum over noisy estimates leans high; the specification leaves the planning method open, and for a hard grouping solved by value iteration the value it promised minus what later bars paid shows that optimism.
metrics.baseline: a gap of zero, meaning the abstract model's promise was kept

metrics.why: This applies once the grouping is made hard, as in the specification's Hard-Partition variant. If nearly every bar falls into one abstract state the encoder has collapsed to a point, which the specification notes minimises the distance loss trivially while destroying the structure.

This applies when the plan is solved by value iteration on a hard grouping, which the specification does not name as its planning method. The largest change between the last two sweeps proves the table is the optimum of the abstract model it was given; it says nothing about whether that abstract model matches the market.

The encoder is the one part of this specification fitted by gradient descent, on the squared error between latent distance and the bisimulation target together with the reward and transition fits, so the distance, reward and transition terms are drawn as separate curves per step; they show whether the joint fit settled and never score the model.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: It measures the engine's trading rule and costs and is reported as run; natively the model is a grouping of states and a value table.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: It is computed from a traded equity curve that only the as-run simulation produces.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: It is a property of the traded path and sits in the as-run layer, not in the bisimulation loss.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: It counts closed winning and losing trades, and the abstraction itself closes no trades.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: It is a position-sizing rule rather than a metric and the engine does not compute it.

notApplicable.name: Policy Entropy
notApplicable.why: The policy that comes out of planning on abstract states is greedy and deterministic, so it has no entropy.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette coefficient
notApplicable.why: The groups are defined by matching reward and next-state behaviour, not by compactness in feature space, so a compactness score would grade the wrong property.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable agent trains the encoder so that the absolute-difference distance between two latents matches their reward gap plus the discounted Wasserstein distance between their Gaussian next-latent predictions, then groups the training latents with k-means and runs value iteration on the grouped model; but the transition does not depend on the action and there is no slowly updated target encoder, so the long-minus-short value gap of an abstract state reduces to twice that state's mean training tape move and the planning depth changes nothing in the call. The market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state, so the as-run numbers measure whether the mean move of each abstract state in training carries over to later bars.
asRun.probabilityNote: Each bar is assigned to the nearest k-means centroid of its encoded window, and the probability of up is the sigmoid of that abstract state's long-minus-short table value multiplied by one inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows; the temperature cannot flip the sign, and the output takes one level per abstract state.

stepQuantity.unit: training: squared bisimulation distance error, latent transition likelihood and squared reward error added together in mixed units, with the value table solved after the epoch and not part of the loss; validation: nats per scored validation bar after the temperature fit

meaningful.why: Each abstract state votes long or short by the sign of its mean training tape move, and this is what trading those votes earned on unseen bars after costs under the engine's rule, with the planner's own flat action overridden.
It sets the long-or-short vote of the bar's abstract state against the realised direction in one symmetric number, which tests directly whether states that drifted up in training still do.
If most abstract states inherit the training span's drift the votes are nearly all one side; taking away buy and hold on the same folds shows what the grouping added beyond that.
It relates the per-bar profit of the abstract-state votes to their swing under the engine's always-in-the-market rule, so it grades the vote's sign plus that rule.
It shows the deepest losing stretch of the votes; a bar that stays in one abstract state keeps the same side until the encoded window crosses to another centroid.
A trade ends when the bar moves to an abstract state with the opposite vote, so winning over losing trade money after costs shows whether those state changes were worth acting on.
The share of profitable closed trades describes how the changes of abstract state resolved, read with the trade count because few states mean few flips.
The share of scored bars where the abstract state's vote matched the realised direction, read against the fold's majority-class accuracy since a state's vote is its training-span average.

Every abstract state votes by its training-span average, so the share of scored bars in the fold's training majority class is what the votes earn by following the drift alone, and the accuracy of the abstract-state votes is read against it on the same fold.

A trade closes when the bar moves to an abstract state with the opposite vote or the fold ends, and few abstract states mean few flips, so the count of closed trades shows how many state changes the profit and the win rate rest on.

The best learning-rate trial's search score minus the same quantity on the fold's test walk shows how much of the selection score the abstraction failed to carry to unseen bars; it sits beside the search objective value, which is optimistic by construction.
Averaging the hit rate on up bars and down bars reveals the case where nearly every abstract state votes the same side.

The score takes only as many levels as there are abstract states, so the curve has a few points; it still shows whether states with a larger mean training move went up more often, but it is read as a coarse check.

The forecast is the mean training price target of the bar's abstract state, from a second fit whose reward is the price target; skill against forecasting no move tests whether the grouping separates bars by the size and sign of what follows.
The average miss in points of the abstract-state mean move, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars; with few states the forecast is a short staircase.
Whether the sign of the abstract state's mean target matched the move; it comes from a separately fitted encoder and grouping, so it can disagree with the traded vote.
The share of bars sitting in long-voting abstract states shows whether the grouping produced two-sided calls or one drift-following side.
The number of distinct probability values in a fold equals the number of abstract states that test bars actually visited, which tells how coarse every ranking and calibration figure is.
Only the learning rate is searched for this agent, on inner blocks of the training span, and the best trial's score is a selection score that is optimistic by construction.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The probability is a value gap pushed through one temperature fitted on validation rows, a preference with a scale chosen afterwards, so its logarithmic loss does not grade a forecast probability of this model.
The squared distance to the outcome grades the fitted temperature on a handful of levels more than anything the abstraction learned.
With one level per abstract state and a single temperature fitted on validation, the bins hold a few points whose position reflects that temperature.
The slope of the outcome on the log-odds is exactly what the single validation temperature was fitted to set, so it reports the fit and not the model.
The spread of the probability is set by the validation temperature multiplying the value gaps; a temperature near zero flattens every state to one half whatever the grouping found.
The training curve is the summed distance, transition and reward loss and the validation curve is logarithmic loss after the temperature fit, so their difference compares unrelated quantities.
With long-only off and no stop or target the engine never goes flat after the first call, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the planner's flat action.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state.
The planner's flat action, its sizing and its holding period are overridden: the engine trades every bar long or short by the sign of the abstract state's value gap.
Because the abstract transition does not depend on the action, the discount factor and the value iteration do not change which side a state votes; only the state's mean training tape move does.

The agent is trained on the move from the next bar's open to the open after the holding period, net of the round-trip cost, while the classification metrics score the close-to-close move over the label horizon.

The inverse temperature is fitted on the validation rows and the kept epoch is the one with the best validation reward, so validation numbers are partly in sample and only the test walk is out of sample.
The k-means grouping is refitted after every epoch on that epoch's training latents, so abstract state labels are not comparable between epochs or folds without alignment.
The price forecast is the abstract state's mean training target from a second fit of the encoder and grouping, not from the weights that produce the traded call.
The probability may take only a few levels, one per visited abstract state.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because horizons overlap, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq future the cost charged is the Micro Nasdaq account figure, applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.

hierarchical_latent_variable_model.summary: A two-level variational autoencoder: a slow latent from the whole window and a fast latent from its last bars conditioned on it; an actor-critic reads both.
hierarchical_latent_variable_model.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the actor-critic's share of long over long + short on [slow; fast] latent means; the market does not react to the agent, so it maximises cost-aware reward on the training span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost) with its own position left out of its state. Differs from the spec: the latents describe market context, not skills to transfer between tasks. Expect: a slow and a fast market summary; edge only from learned feature dynamics.

native.produces: Two stacked hidden summaries of the bars, a slow one read from a long window and a fast one read from a short window given the slow one, together with a decoder that rebuilds the bars from them and a lower bound on how probable the model finds those bars.
native.targetVariable: The feature rows of a window of bars, described as coming from a slow hidden variable and a fast hidden variable that depends on the slow one.
native.objectiveNote: The bound carries two Kullback-Leibler divergence penalties, one holding the slow summary near a fixed prior and one holding the fast summary near a prior that is itself computed from the slow summary, and both penalty weights are ramped up from near zero so that neither level is ignored early in training.

metrics.why: The two-level model is trained to make real windows of bars probable, so its own score is the evidence lower bound on windows it never trained on, reported as a lower bound and with both penalty weights at their final values.
metrics.baseline: The same bound from the same model with the slow summary removed, on the same held-out windows.

metrics.why: The decoder rebuilds the bars from the slow and fast summaries together, and the share of feature variance it fails to rebuild on unseen windows shows how much of the tape the two summaries actually carry.
metrics.baseline: One, which is the error of rebuilding every row as the feature averages.

metrics.why: The reason for stacking a slow summary above a fast one is that the pair describes bars better than a single flat summary of the same total size, so the bound has to be compared with that flat version on the same folds.
metrics.baseline: The same encoder and decoder with one flat hidden summary whose size equals the slow and fast sizes added together.

metrics.why: Reported separately for the slow level and the fast level, a divergence near zero at either level means that level's encoder has stopped reading the bars and is just returning its prior.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value for a level whose encoder ignores the bars completely.

metrics.why: The specification names collapse of either level as the central training difficulty, and counting the slow units and the fast units whose value actually changes from window to window shows directly how much of each level survived.
metrics.baseline: The configured size of the slow summary and of the fast summary.

metrics.why: The specification warns that this model can memorise sequences, which appears as the bound on training windows being far better than the same bound on validation windows once both penalty weights have finished ramping.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value when the two-level model describes unseen windows as well as the windows it trained on.

metrics.why: The specification proposes grouping the slow summary into market regimes, and those groups are only usable if a refit of the same model on a neighbouring fold sorts the shared bars into the same groups.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the agreement expected between two unrelated groupings of the same bars.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The specified model rebuilds bars from two hidden summaries and never takes a position, so this ratio describes the trading rule the Model Cycle adds on top and not the model.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: It needs a per-bar profit series from filled trades, and the two-level model produces summaries and rebuilt bars, not trades.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: A drawdown is read from an equity curve, and nothing in a model trained on the evidence lower bound produces an equity curve.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: It is a ratio of winning to losing closed trades, and the specified model closes no trades because it outputs no action.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: This is a position sizing rule built on an assumed edge, not a measurement of how well the slow and fast summaries describe the bars.

notApplicable.name: Policy Entropy
notApplicable.why: The specified model has no policy, since its outputs are two hidden summaries and a rebuilt window, so there are no action odds whose spread could be measured.

notApplicable.name: Mean test-tape return of the policy's own action
notApplicable.why: As specified the model outputs hidden summaries and rebuilt bars and takes no position, and an action appears only when a separate policy is attached on top of the two summaries.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The model states how probable a window of bars is, not how likely the next move is to be up, so there is no up or down probability of its own to score.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter does build the two-level variational autoencoder, with a slow summary read from the whole window and a fast summary read from its last bars given the slow one, but it adds a head that predicts the scaled open-to-open price move over the label horizon from the two summary samples, as an auxiliary training loss that shapes the summaries, and an actor-critic that reads the detached summaries and picks short, flat or long from the two summary means, trained on that move net of one round trip, so the as-run numbers measure that added trading agent and not the fit of the bars; the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the actor's share of long out of long plus short, which is the logistic function of the long score minus the short score, read from the slow and fast summary means of the current window with no sampling and no fitting against outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: training is a unitless sum of squared rebuilding error, squared price move error of the added head, weighted Kullback-Leibler divergence and actor-critic loss, and validation is nats

meaningful.why: The actor-critic on the two summaries is trained to collect cost-aware reward on the training tape, so the dollars its long or short call earns after costs on the test bars is the closest engine number to what it was trained for.

The actor leans long when the slow and fast summaries point to a rising horizon move, so the hit rate of that lean on up bars and on down bars separately tests whether the summaries carry direction at all.
An actor whose long share sits above one half on most bars earns whatever the market drifted, and subtracting buy and hold on the same folds shows what the summaries added beyond that drift.
It puts the per-bar dollars from the actor's calls against their bar-to-bar swings, under the engine's rule that the position follows the sign of the latest call and is never sized by the agent.
It shows the deepest hole the actor's calls dug on the test bars, which matters because the slow summary can hold the agent on one side through a whole adverse stretch.
It compares the dollars won and lost by the closed trades that the actor's call flips produce, read with the trade count because a slow summary that rarely flips yields few trades.
It counts how many of the trades opened by a flip of the actor's lean closed with a gain after costs, and is read beside the average win and average loss.
It is the share of scored bars where the actor's lean toward long or short matched the horizon move, compared with calling the fold's training majority direction on every bar.
It condenses the four cells of the actor's long and short calls against the real moves into one number that stays at zero when the agent simply calls one side all the time.
The long share moves smoothly with the two summaries, so this tests whether bars where the actor leaned harder toward long went up more often, without trusting the size of the share.

The forecast line comes from a second fit of the same two-level model with a head that predicts the horizon move from the slow and fast summaries, so skill against forecasting no change tests whether those summaries hold the size of the move.
It states in points how far the move predicted from the two summaries landed from the real horizon move, and is read against the error of forecasting no move on the same bars.
It checks whether the sign of the move predicted from the summaries matched the real sign, which is a separate fit from the actor and can disagree with the traded call.
The entropy bonus holds the actor's long share close to one half, so a small tilt decides every call, and the share of bars called up shows whether the agent has become one-sided.
Trades open only when the actor's lean crosses one half, so the count shows how often the slow and fast summaries actually changed the agent's mind on the test bars.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The long share is a preference shaped by reward and pulled toward one half by the entropy bonus, so grading its size as the odds of an up move scores a forecast the actor never made.
For the same reason the squared gap between the actor's long share and the outcome measures how strongly the entropy bonus flattened the policy, not how honest a probability is.
Nearly every long share falls in the two bins beside one half, and the share was never fitted to outcome frequencies, so the binned gap describes the policy's flatness.
The training curve holds the summed model and actor-critic loss while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference compares two unrelated quantities.
With long only off and no stop or target the engine is always in a position once the first call is made, so this describes the engine's rule and overrides the actor's own flat action.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and its own position is not in its state, so each bar's call depends only on the window of features ending at that bar.

The actor has a flat action, but the engine trades long when the long share is at least one half and short otherwise, so the agent's own choice to stand aside, its sizing and its holding period are overridden.

The kept epoch is the one with the highest mean net reward on the validation bars for a position equal to twice the long share minus one, so the validation reward of that epoch is optimistic and only the test walk is out of sample.
The price forecast is a separate fit of the same two-level model with a move head and no actor, kept on validation Huber loss, so its line and the traded call come from two different sets of weights.

This world model is not action-conditioned and has no step-ahead transition: it rebuilds the window's average feature row and its last feature rows and predicts the price move over the label horizon from the two summaries, with no step-ahead transition on prices or summaries.
Horizon moves of neighbouring bars overlap, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and not a simple binomial interval.

The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open, and costs for roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract reuse that contract's account figures as a stated assumption.
Only the learning rate is searched, and the search score is the same per-bar Sharpe ratio objective used for every model, which is optimistic by construction.

dreamer.summary: An RSSM world model and, trained together with it, an actor and critic that learn only from imagined rollouts of the latent prior started at real states (lambda-returns).
dreamer.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the actor's share of long over long + short at the window's posterior state; the market does not react to the agent, so it maximises cost-aware reward on the training span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost) with its own position left out of its state. Differs from the spec: Gaussian latents (no discrete V2 latents); the transition takes no action; rewards score every action at each imagined state. Expect: imagination adds no information beyond the learned feature dynamics.

native.produces: A recurrent state-space world model that carries a deterministic memory and a sampled latent for every bar, plus an actor that outputs a stochastic policy over position actions and a critic that outputs a value estimate, both trained on rollouts imagined inside that latent space.
native.targetVariable: The discounted sum of future trading reward the actor expects to collect from the current latent state, with the world model's own statements being the next latent state, the rebuilt observation, the reward and the continuation flag.
native.objectiveNote: Dreamer's version trains the world model on reconstruction, reward prediction and a Kullback-Leibler term between the posterior and prior latent, and trains the actor on the bootstrapped lambda-return of rollouts imagined from real starting states plus an entropy bonus; in the specification the recurrent transition is action-conditioned and predicts latent states, which a decoder can render back to observations.

metrics.why: Dreamer's actor is improved almost entirely on rollouts imagined inside the learned latent space, so the reward its frozen policy collects on unseen real bars is the one number that says whether the dream taught it anything about the market.
metrics.baseline: The same tape with the flat action on every bar, which pays zero, and buy and hold on the same bars.

metrics.why: Every imagined rollout steps the prior forward with no new bar to correct it, so the error of the latent prediction at each step up to the imagination horizon shows how many dreamed steps the actor can trust before the dream drifts from the tape.
metrics.baseline: The same recurrent model predicting that the latent state stays where the last real bar left it.

metrics.why: The actor is paid in rewards from the world model's reward head, so comparing the return it dreamed with what the same policy earned on real bars exposes a world model that is over-confident outside the training regime, the overfitting risk the specification names.

The reward head reads the same deterministic memory and sampled latent the actor reads, so its forecast of the coming move against forecasting no move tests whether the latent state carries any information the dreamed rewards could be built on.
metrics.baseline: The no-change forecast on the same resolved bars.

metrics.why: Dreamer samples its latents, its imagined rollouts and its actions, so two seeds dream different tapes and the spread of the test reward across seeds tells a real edge from one lucky dream.

The divergence between the posterior latent, which has seen the bar, and the prior latent, which has not, is the part of the world-model loss that spikes early and collapses late; near zero the sampled latent is ignored and imagination runs on the deterministic memory alone.

The actor is paid an entropy bonus so it does not lock onto one position action early in imagination; entropy that falls to zero means the dreamed rewards pushed it to a single action, and entropy that never falls means the bonus outweighs every dreamed reward.
metrics.baseline: The logarithm of the number of position actions, which is the entropy of choosing among them evenly.

metrics.why: The critic supplies the value beyond the fixed imagination horizon inside every lambda-return, so a critic that explains none of the variation in those returns leaves the actor chasing only the few dreamed steps it can see.

The kept Dreamer weights are the epoch whose actor earned the most on the validation tape, a maximum over epochs that flatters itself, so it is shown beside the test reward and never read as the result.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: It never applied natively because the agent's own yardstick is reward per decision; the Sharpe ratio appears in the as-run record as a measure of the engine's rule trading the actor's lean.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: It is computed from the engine's per-bar equity and never from anything the world model or the actor outputs, so it is an as-run figure only.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: The drawdown belongs to the simulated account path of the run and is reported in the as-run record, not as a native property of Dreamer.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: Winning and losing trades exist only after the engine turns the bar-by-bar action into entries and exits, so the ratio is as-run only.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: A sizing formula is a decision rule and not a performance metric, and nothing in Dreamer's training or in the engine computes it.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss of the long share
notApplicable.why: The actor's long share is a preference shaped by reward and by the entropy bonus, not a forecast probability fitted by likelihood, so a logarithmic score of it grades nothing Dreamer was trained to state.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction error as the score
notApplicable.why: The decoder can rebuild a bar's features well from a latent state that is useless for choosing a position, so reconstruction is a training term and not the grade of the agent.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable Dreamer keeps the recurrent state-space model and trains the actor and critic jointly with it on imagined rollouts, but the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state: the transition takes no action, so one rollout of the Gaussian prior is imagined and the reward head scores short, flat and long at every imagined state; the latents are Gaussian with no categorical variant, and the world is the fixed training price tape with next-open fills and a round-trip cost. The as-run numbers therefore measure whether the actor's long-over-short lean at the window's posterior state matches the direction of the move over the label horizon, not an agent acting in a responsive environment.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the actor's probability of long divided by its probability of long plus short, which equals the sigmoid of the long logit minus the short logit, read at the posterior mean state of the bar's window with the flat action dropped and no curve fitted afterwards.

stepQuantity.unit: training is the world-model loss plus the actor loss plus half the critic loss in mixed units; validation is in nats

meaningful.why: It tests whether the lean the actor learned from dreamed rewards, long when its long share is at least one half and short otherwise, makes money after costs on bars it never trained on, with the engine overriding its flat action, its sizing and its holding period.

The long share is a continuous sigmoid of the actor's logit gap, so this ranking number tests whether bars where the actor leans harder long really went up more often, without trusting the scale the entropy bonus squeezed toward one half.
It sets the actor's traded lean against simply holding the same contract over the same folds, which shows whether the imagination-trained policy added anything beyond the drift of the series.

It grades the per-bar profit of the engine's rule driven by the actor's lean against its own variability, a statement about the lean under that rule and not about the reward the actor optimised in its dream.
It shows the deepest hole the account fell into while the engine followed the actor's lean, a risk the actor never saw because its dreamed reward is paid decision by decision with no account path.
It compares the dollars won with the dollars lost on the trades the engine closed when the actor's lean flipped, which tests whether the flips are worth their round-trip costs.
It counts how many of the engine's closed trades made money, and is read beside the trade count because a trade here ends when the actor's lean flips rather than after each decision.

native.produces: SimPLe produces a stochastic policy over position actions that was trained by an ordinary model-free learner almost entirely inside a learned simulator of the bars, and the simulator itself is used only for training and is not consulted when the policy acts.
native.targetVariable: For the simulator, the next observed bar and the reward given recent bars and the action; for the policy, the discounted sum of rewards it collects inside simulated episodes
native.objectiveNote: The simulator is fitted by maximum likelihood with scheduled sampling, which feeds it its own predicted bars in place of real ones more and more often, and the policy is then trained by an unmodified policy-gradient learner against the frozen simulator; the model is conditioned on the action and predicts full observed bars, not a latent code.

metrics.why: The policy has practised almost only on bars the simulator invented, so the test that matters is the reward its own actions collect on real later bars that neither the simulator nor the policy learner was fitted on.
metrics.baseline: The reward of staying flat on the same test tape, which is zero, and the reward of holding long on every bar of that tape

metrics.why: Simulated episodes roll the model forward on its own sampled bars for the whole rollout length, so the error of the predicted bar and reward at each step ahead shows how long an episode can run before the policy is training on fiction, which is what the rollout cap is set against.
metrics.baseline: The error of predicting that the bar's features do not change over the same number of steps on the same bars

metrics.why: A policy trained inside a simulator learns to use the simulator's flaws as if they were edge, so its mean reward in simulated episodes minus its mean reward on the real tape is the direct measure of how much of what it learned was an artefact.

The simulator's sampled bars, the starting states of simulated episodes and the policy learner's own action draws all depend on the seed, and policy-gradient learning inside a noisy simulator is high-variance, so the spread of test reward across seeds is part of the result.
metrics.baseline: The same agent on the same series with only the seed changed

metrics.why: The policy learner keeps a real probability over actions, and when that probability collapses onto one action after a few simulated cycles it usually means the policy found a deterministic quirk of the simulator rather than a pattern in the bars.
metrics.baseline: The entropy of choosing short, flat and long equally often, which is the natural logarithm of three

metrics.why: When the inner learner is an actor-critic method its value function is fitted only to simulated returns, so the share of return variance it explains inside the simulator shows whether the advantage signal driving the policy is information or noise.
metrics.baseline: A value function that predicts the mean simulated return for every state, which explains none of the variance

metrics.why: The cycle of simulator fitting and simulated policy training whose policy is kept is the one that earned most on the validation bars, so that validation reward is the top of a list of cycles and reads higher than the same policy will earn on fresh bars.
metrics.baseline: The same kept policy's reward on the fold's test tape

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The policy learner maximises discounted simulated reward and the simulator maximises likelihood, neither of which is a ratio of mean to spread, so a Sharpe ratio appears only once the engine trades the policy's calls on real bars.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: Downside-adjusted return describes a traded equity path under a stated fill rule, which belongs to the layer where the policy's calls are actually traded and not to training inside the simulator.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: Simulated episodes are short and their reward is summed with no memory of an equity peak, so drawdown is a property of the engine's trading of the calls and not of the learned policy.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: Profit factor counts closed winning and losing trades, and the policy emits a position action per bar with no notion of a trade until an outside rule opens and closes them.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: A Kelly fraction is a sizing rule fed by an estimated edge and odds, while this policy chooses among fixed-size position actions, so the row is neither a metric nor a part of the method.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The policy's probability of choosing long is a preference shaped by simulated reward and an entropy bonus, not a stated chance that the market closes higher, so grading it as odds would test something the policy never claimed.

notApplicable.name: Held-out reconstruction error as the score
notApplicable.why: The simulator can predict the next bar's features closely while its reward output is useless for training a policy, so one-step reconstruction alone would grade the wrong property of the model.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter does alternate fitting a stochastic simulator with scheduled sampling and training a proximal policy optimisation learner only inside simulated episodes, but the market does not react to the agent and its own position is left out of its state: the simulator predicts the next feature row and the tape's move from the window alone, the action enters only as position times predicted move minus cost, and collecting fresh real data is a replay of the same training tape; the as-run numbers therefore measure whether the policy's lean toward long on a real window matches the later move, and whether trading that lean makes money.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the copied-out policy network's probability of long divided by its probability of long plus short on the real window of recent feature rows, with nothing fitted to outcomes, so it is the policy's lean and not a calibrated chance.

stepQuantity.unit: on training rows the simulator's loss per window (the Gaussian negative log-likelihood of the next feature row plus the squared errors of its reward output on the real and on the scheduled-sampling window, in mixed units); on validation rows nats per scored bar of the long share

meaningful.why: The policy was trained to collect reward net of costs inside the simulator, so net profit on the walked test bars is the closest engine number to its goal and the first place where the simulator's inventions are replaced by real fills.

The engine takes from the policy only whether it leans long or short on each real window, and averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars tests whether that lean separates the two outcomes or merely repeats one side learned in simulation.

A simulator fitted on a rising training tape predicts positive moves and teaches the policy to lean long, so the profit left after subtracting holding long through the same folds shows whether simulated practice found anything beyond the drift.
It restates the profit of the policy's long-or-short lean per unit of bar-to-bar swing, and the level of zero is only an arithmetic marker because a trader with no skill still pays costs.
Simulated episodes last only the planning horizon and sum reward with no memory of an equity peak, so the deepest fall of the test equity shows a risk the policy never met in training.
It compares what the winning trades made with what the losing trades gave back after costs, where a trade here ends only when the policy's lean crosses from one side to the other.
The share of closed trades that ended positive is read beside the profit factor, because a policy rewarded on mean simulated reward can win rarely and large or often and small.
It counts how often the side the policy leaned to matched the move, with the cut at one half sitting exactly where its long and short probabilities are equal, since no curve was fitted on top.
One symmetric number for the agreement between the policy's lean and the outcomes, which stays near zero when simulated training has collapsed the policy onto one side for nearly every window.

The long share varies continuously with the window, so this tests whether windows where the policy leaned harder toward long went up more often, a ranking question that does not need the share to be a probability.

The forecast line comes from the simulator network refitted with its reward output pointed at the scaled price move, so this skill against the no-change forecast is the one engine number that grades the simulator's predictive half directly.
The size in points of the miss of the simulator's reward output when it is trained on the price move, read beside the no-change forecast's error on the same resolved bars.

How often the sign of the simulator's forecast matched the move, which can disagree with the traded call because the policy was trained by a separate learner on what a different fit of the simulator imagined.

The simulation cycle whose policy is kept is the one with the highest mean net reward on the validation tape for a position of twice the long share minus one, so this number is the top of a list of cycles and reads optimistic beside the test result.
Shows whether simulated training has left the policy leaning long on nearly every window, in which case every trading number above is close to buy and hold.
The count of flips of the policy's lean, read beside every trading number, because simulated reward charged a cost on every held step while the engine charges only when the call flips.

The search covers only the learning rate shared by the simulator and the policy learner and scores each trial on inner blocks of the training span, so the best trial's score is a selection score and reads optimistic.
The best trial's search score minus the same quantity on the test walk shows how much of the chosen learning rate's apparent edge was the luck of picking the top trial.

The same long share is not a stated chance of an up close, so its squared distance from the outcome reports how strongly the policy commits and not how honest it is.
Nothing in simulated policy training asks the long share to equal the up rate, so the binned gap between the two is not an error of this model.

The training channel holds the simulator's likelihood and reward loss and the validation channel holds the logarithmic loss of the policy's long share, so their difference compares two different quantities and is not an overfitting gap.
The policy has a flat action of its own, but the engine never goes flat once in a trade, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the policy's choice.

The price forecast comes from a second fit of the simulator network with its reward output trained on the price move; its next-row output and reward output share one body, but the traded policy is a separate network that does not share it.
The last reported batch of each cycle carries minus the mean simulated reward of the policy learner, a different quantity from the simulator loss in the other batches of the same curve.
