model_data_ratio.label: Model data ratio
model_data_ratio.description: Weight of imagined transitions against real ones in the actor-critic's loss.

model_error_threshold.label: Model error threshold
model_error_threshold.description: Normalised reward error on the held-out training tail above which imagined data and lookahead are scaled down.

lookahead_weight.label: Lookahead weight
lookahead_weight.description: Weight of the model's one-step action values added to the policy's logits at prediction.

native.produces: A position action and a value estimate from an actor-critic whose updates use a replay buffer holding real transitions mixed with short rollouts of a learned environment model, plus, in the lookahead variant, a short predicted path used to re-rank the candidate actions.
native.targetVariable: The position to hold at each bar, chosen to maximise discounted reward after costs.
native.objectiveNote: The actor and critic receive an ordinary model-free update, but on batches that mix real transitions with model-generated ones at a set ratio that is shrunk when the model's held-out error passes a threshold, while the environment model is fitted separately by regression on real transitions only; that model is action-conditioned because it takes the state and the action, and it predicts the explicit next state and reward, not a latent code.

metrics.why: Mixing imagined transitions into the replay buffer is only worth doing if the actor that results earns more on real bars, so the verdict is the average reward of the frozen actor's own action on bars neither the buffer nor the environment model ever saw.
metrics.baseline: The same agent staying flat on every bar, which earns nothing, and buy and hold on the same series.

metrics.why: The specification itself asks for the mixing ratio to be validated against the pure model-free version, so the same actor-critic is rerun with the simulated share of each batch and the lookahead set to nothing and the difference is what the model half added.
metrics.baseline: The same actor-critic on the same folds with the simulated-to-real mixing ratio at zero and no lookahead.

metrics.why: Rollouts are kept short because one-step mistakes compound, so the error of the environment model at each step ahead of a rollout, measured on held-out real transitions, shows how deep the rollouts can be trusted, while the trust gate itself reads a single held-out one-step error.
metrics.baseline: The persistence forecast that the next state equals the current state, at the same steps ahead.

metrics.why: The failure the specification warns of is a policy that looks excellent inside its own model and disappoints on the tape, and the reward the actor collects in model rollouts minus the reward it collects on real bars measures exactly that.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value when rollouts and the real tape pay the actor the same.

metrics.why: The actor's sampled actions, the minibatches drawn from the buffer and the starting states of the rollouts all depend on the seed, so one run of the mixed update says little until the spread over reseeded runs is seen.
metrics.baseline: The same agent on the same series with only the seed changed.

metrics.why: The critic is the part trained on the blend of real and simulated targets, so how much of the realised return its estimate explains on real bars shows whether the simulated share sharpened it or polluted it.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value of a critic that predicts the mean return for every state.

metrics.why: An actor that exploits a biased environment model tends to pile all its probability on the action the model flatters, and a mean entropy that drops early in training is the warning sign of that collapse.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the number of actions, which is the entropy of choosing among them evenly.

metrics.why: The kept weights are the ones that did best on a later validation block, so that block's reward is flattered by the choosing and is shown only to be read beside the test value.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The registry's Sharpe ratio measures the Model Cycle's trading rule applied to the agent's preferred side, so it lives in the as-run record, while natively the agent is judged by the reward of its own action.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: It is a downside-risk figure of the engine's simulated equity path and belongs to the as-run record, because the specification's reward carries no downside term of its own.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: The drawdown is a property of the equity path the engine builds from the agent's calls and is reported as run, not a quantity the mixed actor-critic update defines.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: It is computed from the engine's closed trades under the engine's holding rule and is an as-run number, since the specification's agent has no trade bookkeeping of its own.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: It is a rule for choosing position size and not a measurement of the agent, and nothing in the specification's training uses it.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The actor's action probabilities are preferences shaped by reward and never claim to equal how often price rises, so scoring them as forecast odds grades something the agent did not state.

notApplicable.name: Held-out reconstruction error
notApplicable.why: The environment model predicts the next state forward in time and has no bottleneck that rebuilds its own input, so there is nothing to reconstruct.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable agent keeps the specification's idea of an actor-critic trained on real rewards mixed with short model rollouts whose weight shrinks when the model errs on held-out bars, plus a model lookahead at prediction, but it has no replay buffer or sampled actions and instead scores every action's known reward on a fixed tape, its single environment model takes no action as input so imagined bars do not depend on what the agent does, and the lookahead is one step from one model and not an ensemble; the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state, so the as-run numbers measure cost-aware direction calls and not a managed position.
asRun.probabilityNote: The actor's scores for short, flat and long are taken from a window encoder, the environment model's predicted move for the same window is added to the long score and subtracted from the short score with the lookahead weight scaled by the model's confidence, and the probability of up is the long share divided by the sum of the long and short shares, with nothing fitted to outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: on training rows a mixed loss, the environment model's next-row negative log-likelihood and squared reward error plus the all-action actor-critic loss on real and imagined rewards in move-scale units; on validation rows nats of the long share

meaningful.why: The actor-critic is trained on the net reward of whole trades from real and model-imagined bars, so the money made by trading the side its lookahead-adjusted scores prefer is the as-run number nearest to what it was trained for, read with the agent's own flat choice overridden.

It shows how evenly the preferred side of the actor plus lookahead earned money per bar after costs, which separates a mix of real and imagined training that found something repeatable from one that was paid by a few stretches of the tape.

An actor trained through a rising stretch can simply learn to prefer long, and taking away what holding the contract over the same folds would have made shows whether the mixed update added anything to that lean.

The reward tape pays every decision as its own separate trade, so neither the real nor the imagined batches ever show the actor a run of losses, and the deepest hole on the marked-to-market path is a risk it was never trained to see.

It sets what the winning trades opened by the actor's preferred side made against what the losing ones gave back after costs, read with the trade count because an actor that seldom changes side closes few trades.

It counts the share of trades opened on a change of the actor's preferred side that closed in profit, which describes the shape of the result while the engine's holding rule and not the agent ends each trade.

The entropy bonus keeps the long and short shares close together, and when the model's predicted move tips that balance back and forth the side flips often, so this turnover shows how much of the result the churn paid away in costs.
It counts how often the lookahead-adjusted long score crossed the short score or a holding period ended in a flip, and every trading number of this agent is read with it.
It shows how often the actor plus lookahead preferred long to short, which exposes an agent that sat on one side for the whole test span instead of responding to the window.

The hard call is up whenever the long share is at least the short share, so the hit rate tests whether the side that real and imagined reward taught the actor to prefer is also the side price went, against calling the fold's training majority direction.

Averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars shows whether the actor's preference really changes with the window or whether a one-sided lean learned from the training span is being credited on a trending test span.
It gives one symmetric number for whether the preferred side of the actor plus lookahead moves with the actual direction, where zero means the preference carries nothing beyond a fixed lean.

The long share is a continuous number driven by the actor's score gap and the model's predicted move, so this checks whether bars with a stronger preference for long are more often up bars, using the ordering alone and not reading the share as odds.

The price line is the reward head of the same kind of environment model the agent imagines with, fitted a second time on the price target, so its skill against forecasting no move tests whether the model the agent leans on can forecast at all.
It states in points the typical miss of the environment model's reward head on the move over the label horizon, read beside the miss of the no-change forecast on the same bars.

It checks the sign of the environment model's own forecast, which knows nothing of costs or of the actor, so it can disagree with the traded side and shows how much of the call the lookahead could have supplied.

The kept epoch is the one whose long share, turned into a position between fully short and fully long, earned the highest mean net reward on the validation tape, so this figure is flattered by the choosing and is read only beside the test result.
It is the score that chose the learning rate, the only searched setting of this agent, on blocks inside the training span, and it is optimistic because it is the best of the trials.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The long share is a preference shaped by reward, by costs, by the entropy bonus and by the added lookahead term and was never fitted to how often price rises, so scoring it as odds measures how sharp the actor is and not how honest.
It grades the long share as a probability of an up bar, while the actor was trained to earn reward, so a good or bad value says nothing about the agent's decisions.
Calibration compares stated odds with observed frequencies, and the actor's action shares were never meant to equal the frequency of up bars.
The slope of outcomes on the log-odds of the long share reads the size of the entropy coefficient and of the lookahead weight, not an over-confident or timid forecaster.
It rests on the Brier score of a preference share and on a hindsight up share of the test bars, so neither half refers to anything the agent stated.
The training curve holds the summed model and actor-critic loss while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference compares two different quantities.
With the long-only setting off the engine never goes flat once in a trade, so this share reflects the engine overriding the agent's flat action and not how often the actor wanted to be in the market.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and the agent's position is not in the state, so each decision is rewarded as one fixed trade over the label horizon and nothing in training resembles managing an open position.

The engine overrides the agent's own flat action, its sizing and its holding period: the traded side is long whenever the long share is at least the short share, even on bars where flat was the actor's most preferred action.

The environment model takes no action as input, so the imagined bars mixed into the actor-critic's batches are the same whatever the actor does and add no information beyond the feature dynamics the model learned from the real bars.

The model's confidence is set from its reward error on the last part of the training span, which the direction fit holds out from the model's own loss, and both the weight of imagined batches and the lookahead weight are scaled by it.

The price line comes from a second fit of the environment model alone on the price target, selected on validation Huber loss, so the price forecast numbers test the model's reward head and say nothing about the actor, the mixing ratio or the lookahead.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because targets overlap across the label horizon, so intervals around these numbers need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than MNQ the costs charged are the MNQ account figures, a stated assumption, and the last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.

imagination_augmented_agent.summary: An environment model imagines one short trajectory per first action (then a distilled rollout policy acts); an LSTM encodes each backwards, and the actor-critic reads the encodings beside a model-free path.
imagination_augmented_agent.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the actor-critic's share of long over long + short; the market does not react to the agent, so it maximises cost-aware reward on the training span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost) with its own position left out of its state. Differs from the spec: imagined model noise is drawn per bar from (seed, bar), so a bar's probability does not depend on its batch. Expect: imagination adds no information beyond the learned feature dynamics.

sequence_length.label: Window bars
sequence_length.description: Bars of history the agent reads at every bar; its state is rebuilt from this window on every call (fixed, never searched).

hidden_size.label: Hidden size
hidden_size.description: Units in the hidden layers and recurrent states.

epochs.label: Epochs
epochs.description: Passes over the training bars (the world model's epochs).

patience.label: Patience
patience.description: Validated epochs without improvement before stopping early.

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: Only the most recent bars of the training span are used (keeps a slow model inside a fold's time).

entropy_coefficient.label: Entropy coefficient
entropy_coefficient.description: Weight of the policy entropy bonus: higher keeps the policy's long share nearer one half.

planning_horizon.label: Rollout bars
planning_horizon.description: Imagined bars in each of the three rollouts (one per first action).

native.produces: A probability for each position action and a value estimate from a head that reads a model-free encoding of the current state side by side with recurrent summaries of several trajectories imagined by a learned environment model under a cheap rollout policy.
native.targetVariable: The position to hold at each bar, chosen to maximise discounted real reward after costs.
native.objectiveNote: The actor and critic are trained with an ordinary model-free loss on real reward, with the gradient flowing back through the rollout encoder, while the environment model is fitted separately by regression on real transitions, so imagination enters only as an input the policy may learn to ignore and the policy never collects reward inside the environment model; the environment model is action-conditioned because it takes the state and the imagined action, and it predicts the explicit next state and reward, not a latent code.

metrics.why: The rollout summaries are extra evidence handed to the policy head, and the only fair test of that evidence is the average reward of the action the frozen head picks on bars neither it nor the environment model trained on.
metrics.baseline: The same agent staying flat on every bar, which earns nothing, and buy and hold on the same series.

metrics.why: Because the head can learn to ignore the imagined trajectories, the agent must be compared with itself after the rollout encoder's inputs are removed, which leaves only the model-free path and shows what imagination actually contributed.
metrics.baseline: The same policy and value head on the same folds reading the model-free encoding alone.

metrics.why: Each trajectory is imagined for a set number of bars with no real bar read along the way, so the environment model's error at every imagined step shows how much of what the rollout encoder summarises is forecast and how much is drift.
metrics.baseline: The persistence forecast that the next state equals the current state, at the same steps ahead.

metrics.why: The rollout encoder can latch onto chance links between imagined shapes and reward, and such links change with the seed of the rollouts and of the sampled actions, so the spread over reseeded runs separates a finding from an accident.
metrics.baseline: The same agent on the same series with only the seed changed.

metrics.why: The value head reads the same joined vector of model-free and imagined encodings as the policy head, so how much of the realised return it explains tells whether that joined vector carries information about what comes next.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value of a value head that predicts the mean return for every state.

metrics.why: The specification adds an entropy bonus to keep the policy head from settling on one action before the rollout encoder has learned anything, and the mean entropy over training shows whether that bonus held.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the number of actions, which is the entropy of choosing among them evenly.

metrics.why: The kept weights are those with the best reward on a later validation block, a figure made rosy by the act of picking it, shown so the gap to the test value can be seen.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The registry's Sharpe ratio grades the Model Cycle's trading rule fed by the policy head's preferred side and so belongs to the as-run record, while the agent's own yardstick is the reward of its chosen action.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: It describes the downside of the engine's simulated equity path and is reported as run, since the actor-critic loss on real reward has no downside measure in it.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: The deepest fall of equity comes from the engine marking the agent's calls to market bar by bar and is an as-run number, not something the imagination architecture defines.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: It is built from trades the engine opens and closes under its own holding rule, so it is listed as run and is not a native measure of the rollout-reading policy.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: It is a way of choosing how much to trade and not a measurement, and the specification's policy head outputs action probabilities without any Kelly step.

notApplicable.name: Imagined minus realised return
notApplicable.why: The policy is trained and paid on real reward only and never acts for reward inside the environment model, so there is no imagined return of the policy to set against the realised one.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The head's action probabilities express what reward taught it to prefer and are not a statement of how often price rises, so a probability score does not apply to them.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable agent keeps the specification's parts, an environment model, a rollout policy distilled from the agent, a recurrent encoder that reads each imagined trajectory backwards and a model-free path joined in front of an actor-critic head, but it imagines exactly one trajectory per first action, its environment model takes no action as input so the imagined bars of the trajectories differ only by their noise draws while their rewards differ by position, that noise is drawn per bar from the seed so a bar's output does not depend on its batch, and every action's known reward is scored on a fixed tape; the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state, so the as-run numbers measure cost-aware direction calls.

It measures how steadily the side preferred by the rollout-reading head earned money per bar after costs, which tells a repeatable reading of the window and its imagined futures from a result carried by a few lucky stretches.
Subtracting what simply holding the contract earned on the same folds shows whether the joined model-free and imagined evidence did more than teach the head to sit long through a rising span.

It compares what the winning trades opened by the head's preferred side made with what the losing ones lost after costs, read with the trade count because a head that rarely changes side closes few trades.

It gives the share of trades opened on a change of the head's preferred side that ended in profit, a description of the result's shape, with the engine's holding rule and not the agent deciding each exit.

The imagined trajectories are rebuilt from the window at every bar with fresh per-bar noise, and when that moves the long and short shares past each other the side flips, so this turnover shows how much the noise in imagination cost in fees.
It counts how often the head's long share crossed its short share or a holding period ended in a flip, and each trading number of this agent is read beside it.
It shows how often the head preferred long to short, which reveals an agent that ignored both its imagined trajectories and its window and stayed on one side throughout.

It checks the sign of the environment model's forecast taken alone, before any rollout is encoded or any cost is charged, so it shows the raw directional content that imagination could pass to the head.

The kept epoch is the one whose long share, turned into a position between fully short and fully long, earned the highest mean net reward on the validation tape, a figure made optimistic by being picked and read only next to the test result.
It is the score that picked the learning rate, the only searched setting of this agent, on blocks inside the training span, optimistic by construction because it is the best trial's value.

action_conditioned_dynamics_transformer.summary: A causally masked transformer over the window's bars and one candidate-action token, trained by teacher forcing to predict each next bar and the action's reward; long and short are scored through the model.
action_conditioned_dynamics_transformer.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is sigmoid of the predicted reward of long minus short, the temperature fitted on validation; the market does not react to the agent, so it maximises cost-aware reward on the training span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost) with its own position left out of its state. Differs from the spec: past action and reward tokens are left out (the agent's position is not state); only the candidate action is a token. Expect: the action matters only through its known reward.

native.produces: A causally masked attention network over a window of alternating bar tokens and position tokens that predicts, at every position token, the next bar's features and the reward of that position, for a planner or an imagination-trained controller to choose positions with.
native.targetVariable: The next bar's feature values and the trading reward that follow each bar and position pair in the window, from which the predicted reward of each candidate position at the latest bar is read.
native.objectiveNote: The network itself is trained only by teacher forcing on squared next-bar error plus squared reward error at every step of the window in one parallel pass, and the choice of position is left to whatever planner or controller reads its predictions; the world model is action-conditioned and predicts the next bar's observed features, price information included, with no latent space.

metrics.why: For lookahead the network is fed its own predicted bars as new tokens, so the error at each further step, in feature units, shows how quickly feeding predictions back into the attention window drifts away from the real bars.
metrics.baseline: The error of repeating the last real bar's features for the same number of steps on the same series.

metrics.why: The network predicts a reward for each candidate position at the latest bar, so the reward actually collected by playing the position it scores highest on unseen bars tests whether the position token carries usable information.
metrics.baseline: Zero reward per decision, which is what staying flat on every bar of the same tape pays.

metrics.why: The reward head reads the position token, so the reward the network promised for the chosen position can be set against what that position really earned, and a positive difference means the promise is optimistic.
metrics.baseline: Zero, which means the predicted reward of the chosen position matched the reward it earned.

metrics.why: The design's point is that the position token changes the prediction, so the next-bar and reward error is compared with the same attention network trained on the bar tokens alone with the position tokens removed.
metrics.baseline: The same network on the same windows with no position tokens.

metrics.why: The teacher-forced squared error is the same quantity on training and validation windows, and an attention network of this capacity can memorise specific bar sequences, so the difference between the two is the memorisation check the specification asks for.
metrics.baseline: Zero, which means the windows it never saw are predicted as well as the windows it trained on.

metrics.why: Each prediction can look directly at any earlier bar in the window, and the spread of its attention weights shows whether it reads the whole window or only the latest bar, in which case the long window buys nothing.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the number of tokens the prediction may attend to, which is the value for perfectly even attention.

metrics.why: The summed squared next-bar and reward error per step shows whether the warm-up and decay schedule the specification stresses let the attention stack settle, and it says nothing about trading quality.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: It measures a trading rule and its costs, which exist only once the predictions are turned into positions and traded.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: It is a trading-rule ratio on losing bars and says nothing about the predicted bars or rewards.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: The worst equity fall is set by the sizing and exit rule around the network and not by the network.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: The network defines no closed trades to sum winners and losers over.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: It is a sizing formula applied after a model is judged and not a score of this model.

notApplicable.name: Policy Entropy
notApplicable.why: The network has no stochastic policy, because it predicts bars and rewards and leaves the choice of position to another part.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Natively nothing states the odds of an up move, because the outputs are a predicted bar and a predicted reward per position.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter builds the causally masked attention network and trains it by teacher forcing on the next bar's features, but past position and reward tokens are left out and only one candidate position token is appended after the window's bars, so the position can change nothing except its own predicted reward; long and short are each scored through the network and the as-run numbers measure the sign and size of that predicted reward difference, which is in effect a forecast of the horizon move net of costs; the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the logistic function of the network's predicted reward of long minus its predicted reward of short at the latest bar, multiplied by one inverse temperature that is fitted by likelihood on the validation rows and held at zero or above.

stepQuantity.unit: training is a unitless sum of the squared next-bar feature error and the squared error of the predicted rewards of short, flat and long, and validation is nats

meaningful.why: The reward head is trained on the cost-aware reward of long and of short on the training tape, so the dollars earned after costs by trading the side with the higher predicted reward on the test bars is the engine number closest to what the network was trained to predict.

The call is long whenever the predicted reward of long exceeds that of short, so the hit rate of that comparison on up bars and on down bars separately tests whether the position token's reward prediction carries direction or just leans one way.

The temperature only stretches the predicted reward difference without reordering it, so this tests the network's own ordering: whether bars with a larger predicted advantage for long went up more often.

A network whose predicted reward of long stays above that of short on most bars simply earns the market's drift, and subtracting buy and hold on the same folds shows what the attention over the window added beyond that.

It sets the per-bar dollars from the higher-predicted-reward side against their bar-to-bar swings, under the engine's rule that the position follows the sign of the latest call and is never sized by the predicted reward.
It shows the deepest equity hole dug by following the predicted reward difference on the test bars, which is where a network that memorised training windows shows its cost.
It is the share of scored bars where the side with the higher predicted reward matched the horizon move, read against calling the fold's training majority direction on every bar.
It folds the four cells of the higher-predicted-reward side against the real direction into one number that stays at zero when the reward difference keeps one sign on every bar.

The forecast line comes from a second fit of the same attention network in which a head on the last bar token predicts the horizon move, so skill against forecasting no change tests whether the window read through attention holds the size of the move.

It compares the dollars won and lost by the trades that open when the predicted reward difference changes sign, and is read with the trade count because a difference that rarely changes sign gives few trades.
It counts how many of the trades opened by a sign change of the predicted reward difference closed with a gain after costs, and is read beside the average win and average loss.
It states in points how far the move predicted from the last bar token landed from the real horizon move, and is read against the error of forecasting no move on the same bars.
It checks the sign of the move predicted by the second fit's head on the last bar token, which is trained apart from the reward head behind the traded call and can disagree with it.

The share of bars on which the predicted reward of long beat that of short shows whether the network has become one-sided, and it reads as every bar called up when the fitted inverse temperature is zero.
A trade closes only when the predicted reward difference changes sign or a fold ends, so the count shows how often the attention network changed its mind on the test bars.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The size of the probability is a predicted reward difference stretched by one number fitted on validation rows, so its logarithmic loss grades that single stretch and not odds the network ever stated.
The squared gap between the stretched reward difference and the outcome mostly reflects how large the fitted inverse temperature came out, which is not a property of the attention network.
A single stretch with no offset cannot correct a lean in the predicted reward difference, so the binned gap describes the fitted temperature and the bins it happens to fill.
The slope is the very quantity the inverse temperature was fitted to set on the validation rows, so on test bars it measures how well that one number carried over.

The training curve holds the summed squared next-bar and reward error while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the stretched reward difference, so their difference compares two unrelated quantities.
With long only off and no stop or target the engine is always in a position once the first call is made, so this describes the engine's rule and not the network's choices.

caveats: The network predicts a reward for staying flat as well, but the engine trades long or short on every bar, holds for the configured holding bars and uses a fixed contract count, so the agent's own flat choice, sizing and holding period are overridden.
The inverse temperature is refitted on the validation rows at every epoch and the validation logarithmic loss shown for that epoch is scored on those same rows, so the validation curve is optimistic.

The kept epoch is the one with the highest mean net reward of the stretched call on the validation tape, not the lowest validation loss on the chart, so the starred epoch need not be the lowest point of the validation curve.
When the fitted inverse temperature is zero the probability of up equals one half on every bar and the engine reads every bar as a long call.

Targets of neighbouring bars share future bars because the label horizon spans several bars, so any interval on these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For instruments other than the Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 the cost per side is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
The hyperparameter search tunes the learning rate only, on the per-bar Sharpe ratio of inner blocks of the training span, which is a selection score and not this network's own loss.

neural_ode_dynamics_learner.summary: An ODE-RNN: between bars the latent follows a learned differential equation integrated over the real elapsed time (torchdiffeq), and each bar updates it through a GRU cell; an actor-critic reads the latent.
neural_ode_dynamics_learner.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the actor-critic's share of long over long + short; the price model integrates to the label horizon and decodes the return; the market does not react to the agent, so it maximises cost-aware reward on the training span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost) with its own position left out of its state. Differs from the spec: no action input to the derivative. Expect: continuous time matters only across session gaps; bars inside a session are evenly spaced.

sequence_length.label: Window bars
sequence_length.description: Bars of history the agent reads at every bar; its state is rebuilt from this window on every call (fixed, never searched).

hidden_size.label: Hidden size
hidden_size.description: Units in the hidden layers and recurrent states.

latent_dimension.label: Latent dimension
latent_dimension.description: Size of the learned latent state.

epochs.label: Epochs
epochs.description: Passes over the training bars (the world model's epochs).

patience.label: Patience
patience.description: Validated epochs without improvement before stopping early.

maximum_training_bars.label: Maximum training bars
maximum_training_bars.description: Only the most recent bars of the training span are used (keeps a slow model inside a fold's time).

entropy_coefficient.label: Entropy coefficient
entropy_coefficient.description: Weight of the policy entropy bonus: higher keeps the policy's long share nearer one half.

differential_equation_solver.label: Solver
differential_equation_solver.description: Fixed-step torchdiffeq solver (four steps per interval); adaptive solvers would make a bar's answer depend on its batch.

native.produces: A hidden state that flows continuously in time under a learned rate-of-change network, integrated by a numerical solver over the real time between observations, with a decoder that turns the state reached at any requested future time into a predicted bar and reward.
native.targetVariable: The next observed bar's feature values and the trading reward at the real timestamp of that bar, however long after the current bar it arrives.
native.objectiveNote: The rate-of-change network is trained by integrating the hidden state across each real gap between bars and charging the squared error of the decoded next bar and reward, and the specification leaves the choice of position to a planner or controller that reads those predictions; the world model is action-conditioned, because the position is an input to the rate of change, and it evolves a latent state that is decoded back to observed features, price information included.

metrics.why: A forecast for any future time is the hidden state integrated that far and decoded, so the error of the decoded bar against the real one as the integration span grows, in feature units, shows how far ahead the learned flow stays close to the market, reported apart for ordinary bar spacing and for session gaps.
metrics.baseline: The error of carrying the last real bar's features forward unchanged over the same span of time on the same series.

metrics.why: The whole case for a continuous-time state is the irregular gap, so the prediction error across weekends and missing bars is compared with the same network told that every gap is one ordinary bar interval, which switches the real elapsed time off.
metrics.baseline: The same network on the same bars with every elapsed time replaced by one bar interval.

metrics.why: The learner itself only predicts, so this needs a controller reading its hidden state, and the reward that controller's position collects on unseen bars then shows whether the continuous-time state holds anything worth trading on.
metrics.baseline: Zero reward per decision, which is what staying flat on every bar of the same tape pays.

metrics.why: The position enters the rate of change, so the reward predicted for a position by integrating the state forward can be set against what the position really earned, and the difference shows whether the flow flatters the positions it is asked about.
metrics.baseline: Zero, which means the reward predicted for the position matched the reward it earned.

metrics.why: Every prediction passes through the encoder into the hidden state and back out through the decoder, so the share of feature variance lost on that round trip alone, with no time elapsed, separates a poor code from a poor flow.
metrics.baseline: The features' total variance on the same unseen bars, which is the loss of rebuilding every bar as the average bar.

metrics.why: The squared error of the decoded next bar and reward is the same quantity on training and validation spans, and an unrestrained rate-of-change network extrapolates wildly over long gaps, so a validation error far above training error flags it.
metrics.baseline: Zero, which means unseen intervals are predicted as well as the intervals it trained on.

metrics.why: The summed squared error per step shows whether the solver tolerance and the restraint on the size of the rate of change let the fit settle, and it says nothing about trading quality.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: It measures a trading rule and its costs, which exist only once the predictions are turned into positions and traded.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: It is a trading-rule ratio on losing bars and says nothing about the continuous-time state or its forecasts.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: The worst equity fall is set by the sizing and exit rule around the learner and not by the learner.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: The learner defines no closed trades to sum winners and losers over.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: It is a sizing formula applied after a model is judged and not a score of this model.

notApplicable.name: Policy Entropy
notApplicable.why: The learner has no stochastic policy, because it predicts future states and leaves the choice of position to another part.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter builds a hybrid in which the hidden state flows under the learned rate of change across the real elapsed time between bars and is then corrected by a gated recurrent cell at each bar, but the position is not an input to the rate of change, and an actor-critic that picks short, flat or long from the final hidden state is added on top, so the as-run numbers measure that added trading agent on a state that only tracks the bars; inside a session the bars are evenly spaced, so continuous time changes the state only across session gaps; the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the actor's share of long out of long plus short, which is the logistic function of the long score minus the short score, read from the hidden state after the window has been integrated and corrected bar by bar, with no fitting against outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: training is a unitless sum of the squared error of each decoded bar, the squared error of the predicted tape move and the actor-critic loss with its entropy bonus, and validation is nats

meaningful.why: The actor-critic on the integrated hidden state is trained to collect cost-aware reward on the training tape, so the dollars its long or short call earns after costs on the test bars is the closest engine number to what it was trained for.

The actor leans long when the hidden state reached by integrating through the window points to a rising horizon move, so the hit rate of that lean on up bars and on down bars separately tests whether the continuous-time state carries direction at all.

The forecast line comes from a second fit of the same model that integrates the hidden state forward by the label horizon and decodes the move, so skill against forecasting no change is the one engine number that tests the learned flow as a forecaster, which is what the specification is about.
The long share moves smoothly with the hidden state, so this tests whether bars where the actor leaned harder toward long went up more often, without trusting the size of the share.
An actor whose long share sits above one half on most bars earns whatever the market drifted, and subtracting buy and hold on the same folds shows what the integrated state added beyond that drift.
It puts the per-bar dollars from the actor's calls against their bar-to-bar swings, under the engine's rule that the position follows the sign of the latest call and is never sized by the agent.
It shows the deepest hole the actor's calls dug on the test bars, including the bars just after a session gap where the state has been integrated over a long stretch with no bar to correct it.
It is the share of scored bars where the actor's lean toward long or short matched the horizon move, compared with calling the fold's training majority direction on every bar.
It condenses the four cells of the actor's long and short calls against the real moves into one number that stays at zero when the agent simply calls one side all the time.
It compares the dollars won and lost by the closed trades that the actor's call flips produce, read with the trade count because a hidden state that drifts slowly flips the call rarely.
It counts how many of the trades opened by a flip of the actor's lean closed with a gain after costs, and is read beside the average win and average loss.
It states in points how far the move decoded from the state integrated to the label horizon landed from the real horizon move, read against the error of forecasting no move on the same bars.
It checks whether the sign of the move decoded from the forward-integrated state matched the real sign, which comes from a separate fit from the actor and can disagree with the traded call.
The entropy bonus holds the actor's long share close to one half, so a small tilt decides every call, and the share of bars called up shows whether the agent has become one-sided.
Trades open only when the actor's lean crosses one half, so the count shows how often the bar-by-bar corrections to the hidden state actually changed the agent's mind on the test bars.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The long share is a preference shaped by reward and pulled toward one half by the entropy bonus, so grading its size as the odds of an up move scores a forecast the actor never made.
The squared gap between the actor's long share and the outcome measures how strongly the entropy bonus flattened the policy, not how honest a probability is.
Nearly every long share falls in the two bins beside one half and the share was never fitted to outcome frequencies, so the binned gap describes the policy's flatness.
The long share was shaped by reward and an entropy bonus and never by outcome frequencies, so a slope fitted to it rescales a preference and tests no stated odds.

The training curve holds the summed decoding, reward and actor-critic loss while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference compares two unrelated quantities.
With long only off and no stop or target the engine is always in a position once the first call is made, so this describes the engine's rule and not the actor's choices.

caveats: The actor also has a flat action, but the engine trades long or short on every bar, holds for the configured holding bars and uses a fixed contract count, so the agent's own flat choice, sizing and holding period are overridden.

The kept epoch is the one with the highest mean net reward of the long-share position on the validation tape, not the lowest validation loss on the chart, so the starred epoch need not be the lowest point of the validation curve.
The actor-critic is trained on the hidden state with gradients cut off, so the trading reward never shapes the learned flow, which is trained only to decode bars and predict the tape move.

Elapsed time is measured in bar intervals and the solver takes fixed steps, so inside a session every integration covers exactly one interval and the continuous-time part acts only across session gaps.

Targets of neighbouring bars share future bars because the label horizon spans several bars, so any interval on these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For instruments other than the Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 the cost per side is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
The hyperparameter search tunes the learning rate only, on the per-bar Sharpe ratio of inner blocks of the training span, which is a selection score and not this model's own loss.
